title: Oil — Oil Filter Housing Bypass Indicator and Heat Shield Rework
abstract: Installation of a mechanical pop-out bypass indicator on the oil filter housing with a re-profiled heat shield, so that an impending filter bypass is visible at the walk-around.

sections.planning_reason: The differential pressure switch fitted at build annunciates only when the bypass has already opened, by which time unfiltered oil has been through the bearings. Shop analysis of eleven engines removed for bearing distress found that in seven cases the bypass had operated on an earlier sector with no record of it anywhere. A mechanical indicator gives the line engineer a visible warning at about seventy per cent of the bypass differential, which is a full check interval of warning, and it does not depend on the electrical annunciation being serviceable.
sections.description: The oil filter housing mount link is replaced by an item with a boss for the pop-out indicator on the upper face, positioned so that it is visible with the fan cowl open and without a stand. The heat shield kit is re-profiled around the boss and the cowl latch is repositioned by twenty millimetres so that the shield can be removed without disturbing the latch. Barrel nuts are replaced at four positions to give access with a standard socket.
sections.accomplishment_summary: This Service Bulletin is accomplished at an engine shop visit only. Remove the oil filter housing from the gearbox pad in accordance with the engine manual. Install the mount link D7920120683140 with the indicator boss. Install the pop-out indicator and check that it resets with a push. Install the re-profiled heat shield kit SAL498770-46 and reposition the cowl latch VA570633-07 by twenty millimetres. Install the barrel nuts EN664100-11 at the four access positions. Remove the redundant firewall panel kit DUD775751-11. CAUTION: THE PRE-MODIFICATION HEAT SHIELD WILL NOT FIT A POST-MODIFICATION HOUSING. DO NOT MIX THE TWO. Re-install the housing on the gearbox pad and torque to the value in the engine manual. Do a leak check at idle and confirm that the indicator has not tripped. Do AMM-S-79-20-12-200-041-A at the next scheduled opportunity to establish the baseline indicator state.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to SOLANO-30 and SOLANO-34 aircraft with Auran 7720 engines. Aircraft from MSN S01696 onward are post-modification from build. Because the work is done at engine level, an aircraft may carry one modified and one unmodified engine, which is permitted; the walk-around card covers both cases.
sections.material_note: Kit K7920-1006-01 covers one engine and contains the mount link, the indicator, the re-profiled heat shield and the barrel nut set. Lead time is fifteen weeks. The removed mount link is scrapped.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next engine shop visit. No on-wing embodiment is offered.
